comments.author: selfhostmaxxer
comments.text: Tried it this morning. Setup was genuinely one compose file, and the OCR-on-screenshots feature is the sleeper hit — I archive a lot of pages that are basically images of text (menus, event posters, old scanned PDFs) and being able to full-text search those locally is something none of the hosted services give me. Two rough edges: memory spikes during OCR of large PDFs, and the archive list gets slow around a few thousand items.

replies.author: tabhoarder
replies.text: OP here — thanks for the real numbers. The PDF memory spike is known (I'm rasterizing whole pages at too high a DPI before OCR, fix in progress) and the list slowdown is a missing index that ships this week. Issue tracker is at bugs.tabstash.example.com if you hit anything else.

replies.author: selfhostmaxxer
replies.text: Filed both with repro steps. Also: the keyboard shortcuts are excellent and undocumented, which is a very developer thing to do.

comments.author: lambdacurious
comments.text: What's the OCR engine situation? Local models for this vary wildly between 'flawless on clean scans' and 'hallucinates entire sentences on anything with columns'.

replies.author: tabhoarder
replies.text: OP — I run a two-pass setup: a fast classical engine first, and only if its confidence is low do I fall back to a heavier local model. Columns are handled by a layout-detection step before either. It's the fallback path that eats the RAM mentioned above.

comments.author: graveyardofapps
comments.text: I have been burned by read-it-later services shutting down THREE times, taking years of annotations with them each time. At this point self-hosted isn't a preference, it's trauma response. Bookmarked (locally).

replies.author: staticdrift
replies.text: The annotations are the real hostage, always. Losing the article list stings; losing five years of marginalia is why I keep everything in plain files now.

comments.author: devilsproxy
comments.text: Honest question: at what point does a read-it-later app become a personal web archive with extra steps? Because the OCR feature suggests this wants to be the latter, and that's a much harder (and more interesting) product.
